title: Customer handover and continuous improvement
audience: Trainee or new worker on the solar panel cleaning track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and demonstrate customer handover and continuous improvement

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the solar panel cleaning track. Panels are usually mounted on roofs or elevated structures and are connected to DC and AC electrical circuits. Panels can produce voltage in daylight even when the rest of the system is off. Cleaning on this track does not include electrical work, isolation of the system, opening enclosures, or cable or connector repair. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body:
Purpose and learning outcome
After this lesson, the learner can demonstrate customer handover and continuous improvement in a routine cleaning workplace, identify limits of their authority and document the result. The following procedures are examples; always apply the approved site process and task instructions.

Detailed workplace method
Summarise what was completed, what was excluded, any damage or access limitations, and what requires client decision. Use clear factual language; avoid promising a result not verified. Send records only through approved channels. Review repeated failures by task, surface, equipment, time allocation or training need. Propose one specific corrective improvement and check whether the next inspection confirms improvement.

Safety, boundaries and escalation
Before proceeding, confirm the actual work scope, hazards, material or equipment suitability and who can authorise changes. Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside training, or the requested result conflicts with a site instruction. Record facts, not assumptions.

Worked example
Three consecutive office cleans show missed skirting edges. The supervisor checks the route and tool selection, adds a targeted inspection point, coaches the team and measures results on the next three shifts.

Supervised practical
Draft a handover from a mixed pass/fail checklist and analyse a four-week defect log to propose and test a process improvement.

Assessment and corrective feedback
An assessor observes the learner and verifies: Reports accurately, protects privacy and links improvement to measured reinspection outcomes. If any critical safety action is missed, provide coaching and require a new demonstration. Attendance alone is not proof of competence.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Confirm the actual work scope, the hazards, and who can authorise any change before you start.
Summarise what was completed, what was excluded, and any damage or access limits.
List the client decisions still needed, and state them in clear, factual language without promising a result that has not been verified.
Send the handover only through the approved channel.
When failures repeat, review them by task, surface, equipment, time allocation or training need.
Check at the next inspection whether the improvement worked, and record facts rather than assumptions.
Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside your training, or in conflict with a site instruction.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is licensed electrical installation work, and PV DC cables may stay live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. On the Victorian, Western Australian and New South Wales pages checked, plain panel washing is not stated to need a licence, and any electrical work on a PV array is referred to a licensed electrician. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

Records are sent only through approved channels.
Repeated failures are reviewed by cause, and one specific corrective improvement is proposed.
The next inspection confirms whether the improvement worked.
summary: The handover summarises what was completed, what was excluded, any damage or access limits and what needs a client decision, in clear and factual language.
Repeated failures are reviewed by task, surface, equipment, time allocation or training need, and one specific improvement is proposed.
The next inspection checks whether the improvement worked, and records go out only through approved channels.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which evidence or checks are essential when you hand over to the customer and improve continuously?
options: A factual summary of what was completed and excluded, with limitations and client decisions identified
A promise that the result is perfect, without verification and a note that the team can be trusted
A summary that omits the exclusions so the client stays happy and the cost of the job is left out too
Records sent through a personal messaging app, for speed to the client's home address and phone

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen to an unfinished item at customer handover?
options: Complete it without authority and hand over the result and tell the client it is finished
Stop the work, escalate it to the supervisor, and do not hand over the unfinished item as complete
Mark it complete and address it at the next visit and tell the client it is finished
Leave the decision to the client at the next visit, with no record and the crew moves on

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say a handover summary should include?
options: A promise that the result is perfect
Nothing excluded, to keep the client happy
What was completed, what was excluded, any damage or access limitations, and what needs a client decision
